paragraphs: Direct judgment: if you are willing to read drawings and tolerances, operate numerically controlled equipment according to programs and safety checks, and complete inspection and records steadily, this direction is worth testing further. Safe trials use only completely fictional drawings and simulation, without touching real machine tools, cutting tools, or hazardous energy.

Observable signals: whether you can check drawings, materials, and tolerances, whether you can set up and machine according to programs and safety requirements, and whether you can steadily complete dimensional inspection and records; personality labels cannot determine fit or qualification.

Suitable conditions: willing to do equipment operation and precision control over the long term, and able to maintain checking and safety habits through repetitive machining. Caution conditions: if it is hard to bear equipment operation safety responsibility and precision pressure, first compare adjacent directions such as equipment repair or assembly.

Safe work sample (completely fictional drawings and materials): for a fictional part drawing, write out the process and tolerance check points, the program check points, the setup and safety confirmation steps, the first-article and in-process inspection arrangements, and the situations that must be confirmed by an authorized person within 60 minutes; do not use real machine tools or hazardous energy.

entries: Preparation and operation: check the drawing and tolerances, check or write the NC program, and machine after completing setup, tool setting, and safety confirmation.
Inspection and maintenance: complete first-article and in-process dimensional inspection, stop and escalate on anomalies, and keep records and maintain equipment.

paragraphs: Computer numerically controlled tool operators correspond to O*NET 51-9161.00, whose duties are to operate computer-controlled machine tools, equipment, or robots to machine or process parts and workpieces of materials such as metal, plastic, wood, and stone, and who may be responsible for equipment setup and maintenance. This page does not equate operation with independent process approval or equipment modification authorization.

Work context (O*NET Work Context survey, 1—5 scale): characterized by equipment operation, precision requirements, and safety risk, with work performed according to programs and safety standards; specific work context values follow the O*NET Work Context survey.

Abilities and work style: requires drawing reading, dimension, and NC foundations, the ability to operate equipment according to programs and safety requirements, and stopping and escalating on anomalies.

Insufficient evidence: this round did not obtain a preparation level that can be safely extracted for O*NET 51-9161.00 on this page; the research inputs also include the official description, tasks, work context, and interest code (RC). These are not used to infer qualifications, wages, or employment framing in mainland China.
Objects of work: part drawings and tolerances, materials and blanks, NC programs and cutting tools, and equipment and safety conditions.
Checkable outputs: conforming machined parts, program and setup records, first-article and in-process inspection records, and equipment maintenance and anomaly records.

Boundaries: this page covers the NC operation and setup and maintenance of O*NET 51-9161.00 and does not include final process and program approval, equipment modification, or special work authorization.

Adjacent relationships are used only for direction comparison: this occupation centers on NC machining operation, robotics technicians focus on assembling and commissioning automated devices, industrial machinery maintenance workers are responsible for equipment repair, and assemblers are responsible for component and complete machine assembly, and the qualifications and responsibilities of each position are not interchangeable.

When comparing, check item by item: who writes and approves programs, who operates the equipment, who is responsible for repair, and who makes the quality judgment; similar names do not mean identical duties and authorization.
Difference from robotics technicians: the latter focus on the assembly and commissioning of automation and robotic systems; this occupation focuses on NC machining operation.
Difference from industrial machinery maintenance workers: the latter are responsible for equipment repair and upkeep; this occupation is responsible for machining to program and self-inspection.
Difference from assemblers: the latter take component assembly as the core output, not cutting tolerance.
